"""
Framework: Next.js.

Write the opening screen.

reply.question: Before the questions, here's what I read from your app's code. Tell me if any of it looks wrong.

statements.text: Your app is light mode: a very pale grey-blue page background with near-black text on top.
Headings use Inter, a plain neutral sans-serif. It is the only font your app loads.
Body text uses Inter too, loaded from Google Fonts and set once for the whole app.
Your main colour is #4f46e5, a strong blue-violet. It fills the buttons, like "New order".
Your greys lean cool, with a slight blue tint. They come from Tailwind's slate family.
Spacing moves in 4-pixel steps. Every padding and margin in the app is a multiple of 4px.
Corners are softly rounded, one single step of about 8px (0.5rem), on buttons and inputs.
Nothing casts a shadow. Buttons even switch shadows off outright, so the look is flat.

How it is shown: shown as a slider from quiet to bold, with a live preview. They can also type their own size and step, or Skip.

Rules:
- Write for someone who builds software but has no design vocabulary. Short sentences. Say what a choice does and how it will look. A design term is fine only next to its plain meaning.
- Every option and its reason must come from what they told you about their product, in their words.
- Options must be real alternatives that look clearly different from each other.
- Put each option's numbers in its label where it has them (hex, px, ratio).
- Recommend exactly one option.
- Never offer anything on the Avoid line.

Each option is a body text size in px (12 to 20) and the step between heading sizes (a ratio from 1.05 to 1.5). Offer 3 to 5 options from quiet to bold, in that order. Each label names both numbers, like "Balanced: 16px body, headings ×1.2".

reply.question: How big should your body text be, and how far apart should heading sizes step? Drag the slider — left is quiet, right is bold. You can also type your own size and step.

options.label: Quiet: 14px body, headings ×1.1
options.reason: Your spacing is tight (4px) and your shadows are flat, so 14px body fits a lot of text on screen. Headings step up only a little (×1.1), so the page reads even and calm.

options.label: Calm: 15px body, headings ×1.2
options.reason: Tight 4px spacing already packs your page, so 15px body stays compact. A ×1.2 step gives headings a clear but gentle lift above the flat layout.

options.label: Balanced: 16px body, headings ×1.25
options.reason: 16px is the easy-to-read default and pairs well with your Inter type and cool greys. ×1.25 makes headings clearly bigger without shouting on a flat, tight page.

options.label: Bold: 17px body, headings ×1.4
options.reason: 17px body reads large, and ×1.4 lifts headings well above the text. With your tight 4px spacing this fills the screen faster, so fewer items fit at once.

options.label: Loud: 18px body, headings ×1.5
options.reason: 18px body with ×1.5 headings is the boldest setting, where headings feel nearly twice the body. Your flat, tight layout turns dramatic but holds less per screen.

reply.why: Your spacing is tight, shadows flat, greys cool, and everything uses Inter — an even, easy read. 16px body with a ×1.25 heading step fits that: readable, calm, and clear.

The decided foundation:
- surface (light or dark): Light
- display-type (the heading typeface): Inter
- body-type (the body typeface): Inter
- type-scale (type size and weight): 16px body, headings ×1.25. Shown with the reason: 16px is the easy-to-read default and pairs well with your Inter type and cool greys. ×1.25 makes headings clearly bigger without shouting on a flat, tight page.
- brand-color (the brand colour): #3730a3
- secondary-color (a supporting colour): #0f766e. Shown with the reason: Dark teal reads as a clear step away from your indigo and matches your cool greys. Good for small chart lines and secondary buttons on white.
- accent-color (an accent colour): #f59e0b. Shown with the reason: Far from both indigo and teal, so a tiny dot clearly pops on your light screens. Works for 'in progress' or 'needs attention' badges without looking like an error.
- neutral (the greys): Cool
- semantics (success/warning/error colours): #15803d, #b45309, #b91c1c. Shown with the reason: Darker 700 shades match your deep #3730a3 brand and stay far from the amber accent. Strong contrast on white for small text and thin flat icons.
- spacing (density and spacing): Tight, 4px base
- radius (corner rounding): Soft, 8px
- depth (shadows and depth): Flat

reply.summary: Your foundation is built for a light, flat Next.js app that reads cleanly on white. Inter for both headings and body keeps all text in one familiar family, and a 4px spacing rhythm with softly rounded 8px corners gives the product a calm, tidy feel. Deep indigo carries the brand while teal and amber stay reserved for small supporting jobs.
reply.rule: Indigo #3730a3 is the brand colour and belongs on primary buttons, links and active states, never on large background fills or long blocks of body text.

reasons.surface: A light surface suits a flat, tight page and lets your deep #3730a3 and cool greys show at full strength on white.
reasons.display-type: Inter for headings matches your body type, so titles and text look like one family and the app only loads a single font.
reasons.body-type: Inter is a familiar, highly readable screen font that stays clear at 16px in tables, forms and dashboards.
reasons.type-scale: 16px is the easy-to-read default and pairs well with your Inter type and cool greys, and ×1.25 makes headings clearly bigger without shouting on a flat, tight page.
reasons.brand-color: A deep indigo like #3730a3 has enough weight to carry primary buttons and links on white without any shadow or gloss.
reasons.secondary-color: Dark teal reads as a clear step away from your indigo and matches your cool greys, so it works for small chart lines and secondary buttons on white.
reasons.accent-color: Amber is far from both indigo and teal, so a tiny dot clearly pops on your light screens for 'in progress' or 'needs attention' badges without looking like an error.
reasons.neutral: Cool greys sit naturally beside your indigo and teal, keeping borders, captions and disabled states quiet and consistent.
reasons.semantics: Darker 700 shades match your deep #3730a3 brand and stay far from the amber accent, giving strong contrast on white for small text and thin flat icons.
reasons.spacing: A tight 4px base packs more rows and controls on screen, which fits a data-heavy app where users scan a lot at once.
reasons.radius: Soft 8px corners take the hard edge off buttons and cards while staying modest enough for a flat, business-like look.
reasons.depth: Flat surfaces with no shadows keep the page calm and fast, so your indigo, teal and amber carry the meaning instead of drop shadows.
